Foreword
The 2025 yearbook is the
second consolidated volume
covering both observatories
and the first to be compiled
under the joint
data-governance charter. It
merges what were, until last
year, two separately
circulated site reports with
incompatible conventions —
a merger that deliberately
preserves several of those
inconsistencies for archival
fidelity.
Readers should note that Site
ALPHA records retain the
DD.MM.YYYY date
convention of the desert
operations team, while Site
BETA logs use ISO 8601.
Currency figures appear in
the currency of expenditure
— rials, rupees or euros —
with the separator
conventions of the
originating office. Appendix
C provides the conversion
basis.
 «Two deserts of data
— one of sand, one of
 rain — and a single
 instrument:
 patience.»
Programme milestones of the
year include the completion
of aerosol transect T-7, the
first full-season operation of
the cyclone moorings at
BETA, and a 31 per cent
reduction in diesel
dependency at ALPHA.
Setbacks are reported with
equal candour: seventeen
sand-storm shutdowns, one
flooded cable trench, and the
loss of sonde T7-09 to a
fishing trawl.
This volume was compiled by
the Programme Office from
partner submissions received
before 12 January 2026. Late
corrections appear only in
the Annex reprint and are
flagged as non-authoritative.
— The Editors

3 · Desert Operations — Site ALPHA
Site ALPHA operates under the sand-storm shutdown protocol agreed with the regional partner. The
authoritative statement of the protocol, as lodged in Muscat, is reproduced below in the original
Arabic; no English translation is circulated.e3
 Statement 3-1 (Arabic, right-to-left; reproduced as submitted facsimile).
3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.
Crew rotations during the season were staged through the coastal airstrip rather than the desert
track, adding four hours to each rotation but avoiding convoy exposure during peak visibility events.
The protocol threshold (see Statement 3-1) was not breached during any rotation window.
3.1 Dust climatology
Monthly mean dust flux for both sites is mapped in Figure 3-2; the annual maximum at ALPHA
occurred in mid-summer, coincident with the strongest shamal episodes.

3 · Desert Operations — Site ALPHA
Site ALPHA operates under the sand-storm shutdown protocol agreed with the regional partner. The
authoritative statement of the protocol, as lodged in Muscat, is reproduced below in the original
Arabic; no English translation is circulated.e3
 Statement 3-1 (Arabic, right-to-left; reproduced as submitted facsimile).
3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.
Crew rotations during the season were staged through the coastal airstrip rather than the desert
track, adding four hours to each rotation but avoiding convoy exposure during peak visibility events.
The protocol threshold (see Statement 3-1) was not breached during any rotation window.
3.1 Dust climatology
Monthly mean dust flux for both sites is mapped in Figure 3-2; the annual maximum at ALPHA
occurred in mid-summer, coincident with the strongest shamal episodes.

ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.
BETA, 14 June. — Sky the colour of unpolished brass all afternoon. Sun photometer needle
went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and
again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.
Insurance paperwork weighs more than the sonde did. — R.S.

3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.
Crew rotations during the season were staged through the coastal airstrip rather than the desert
track, adding four hours to each rotation but avoiding convoy exposure during peak visibility events.
The protocol threshold (see Statement 3-1) was not breached during any rotation window.

occurred in mid-summer, coincident with the strongest shamal episodes.

12 · Station Diaries (extracts)
ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.
BETA, 14 June. — Sky the colour of unpolished brass all afternoon. Sun photometer needle
went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and

3 · Desert Operations — Site ALPHA
Site ALPHA operates under the sand-storm shutdown protocol agreed with the regional partner. The
authoritative statement of the protocol, as lodged in Muscat, is reproduced below in the original
Arabic; no English translation is circulated.e3
 Statement 3-1 (Arabic, right-to-left; reproduced as submitted facsimile).
3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.
Crew rotations during the season were staged through the coastal airstrip rather than the desert
track, adding four hours to each rotation but avoiding convoy exposure during peak visibility events.
The protocol threshold (see Statement 3-1) was not breached during any rotation window.
3.1 Dust climatology
Monthly mean dust flux for both sites is mapped in Figure 3-2; the annual maximum at ALPHA
occurred in mid-summer, coincident with the strongest shamal episodes.

ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed

again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.

3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.
Crew rotations during the season were staged through the coastal airstrip rather than the desert
track, adding four hours to each rotation but avoiding convoy exposure during peak visibility events.
The protocol threshold (see Statement 3-1) was not breached during any rotation window.

3 · Desert Operations — Site ALPHA
Site ALPHA operates under the sand-storm shutdown protocol agreed with the regional partner. The
authoritative statement of the protocol, as lodged in Muscat, is reproduced below in the original
Arabic; no English translation is circulated.e3
 Statement 3-1 (Arabic, right-to-left; reproduced as submitted facsimile).
3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.
Crew rotations during the season were staged through the coastal airstrip rather than the desert
track, adding four hours to each rotation but avoiding convoy exposure during peak visibility events.
The protocol threshold (see Statement 3-1) was not breached during any rotation window.
3.1 Dust climatology
Monthly mean dust flux for both sites is mapped in Figure 3-2; the annual maximum at ALPHA
occurred in mid-summer, coincident with the strongest shamal episodes.

12 · Station Diaries (extracts)
ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.
BETA, 14 June. — Sky the colour of unpolished brass all afternoon. Sun photometer needle
went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and
again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.
Insurance paperwork weighs more than the sonde did. — R.S.

ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.

went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and

BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean

3 · Desert Operations — Site ALPHA
Site ALPHA operates under the sand-storm shutdown protocol agreed with the regional partner. The
authoritative statement of the protocol, as lodged in Muscat, is reproduced below in the original
Arabic; no English translation is circulated.e3
 Statement 3-1 (Arabic, right-to-left; reproduced as submitted facsimile).
3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.
Crew rotations during the season were staged through the coastal airstrip rather than the desert
track, adding four hours to each rotation but avoiding convoy exposure during peak visibility events.
The protocol threshold (see Statement 3-1) was not breached during any rotation window.
3.1 Dust climatology
Monthly mean dust flux for both sites is mapped in Figure 3-2; the annual maximum at ALPHA
occurred in mid-summer, coincident with the strongest shamal episodes.

12 · Station Diaries (extracts)
ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.
BETA, 14 June. — Sky the colour of unpolished brass all afternoon. Sun photometer needle
went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and
again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.
Insurance paperwork weighs more than the sonde did. — R.S.

3 · Desert Operations — Site ALPHA
Site ALPHA operates under the sand-storm shutdown protocol agreed with the regional partner. The
authoritative statement of the protocol, as lodged in Muscat, is reproduced below in the original
Arabic; no English translation is circulated.e3
 Statement 3-1 (Arabic, right-to-left; reproduced as submitted facsimile).
3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.
Crew rotations during the season were staged through the coastal airstrip rather than the desert
track, adding four hours to each rotation but avoiding convoy exposure during peak visibility events.
The protocol threshold (see Statement 3-1) was not breached during any rotation window.
3.1 Dust climatology
Monthly mean dust flux for both sites is mapped in Figure 3-2; the annual maximum at ALPHA
occurred in mid-summer, coincident with the strongest shamal episodes.

ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310

again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.

Foreword
The 2025 yearbook is the
second consolidated volume
covering both observatories
and the first to be compiled
under the joint
data-governance charter. It
merges what were, until last
year, two separately
circulated site reports with
incompatible conventions —
a merger that deliberately
preserves several of those
inconsistencies for archival
fidelity.
Readers should note that Site
ALPHA records retain the
DD.MM.YYYY date
convention of the desert
operations team, while Site
BETA logs use ISO 8601.
Currency figures appear in
the currency of expenditure
— rials, rupees or euros —
with the separator
conventions of the
originating office. Appendix
C provides the conversion
basis.
 «Two deserts of data
— one of sand, one of
 rain — and a single
 instrument:
 patience.»
Programme milestones of the
year include the completion
of aerosol transect T-7, the
first full-season operation of
the cyclone moorings at
BETA, and a 31 per cent
reduction in diesel
dependency at ALPHA.
Setbacks are reported with
equal candour: seventeen
sand-storm shutdowns, one
flooded cable trench, and the
loss of sonde T7-09 to a
fishing trawl.
This volume was compiled by
the Programme Office from
partner submissions received
before 12 January 2026. Late
corrections appear only in
the Annex reprint and are
flagged as non-authoritative.
— The Editors

ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.
BETA, 14 June. — Sky the colour of unpolished brass all afternoon. Sun photometer needle
went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and
again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.
Insurance paperwork weighs more than the sonde did. — R.S.

12 · Station Diaries (extracts)
ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.
BETA, 14 June. — Sky the colour of unpolished brass all afternoon. Sun photometer needle
went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and
again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.
Insurance paperwork weighs more than the sonde did. — R.S.

fishing trawl.

before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.

went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and
again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.

Foreword
The 2025 yearbook is the
second consolidated volume
covering both observatories
and the first to be compiled
under the joint
data-governance charter. It
merges what were, until last
year, two separately
circulated site reports with
incompatible conventions —
a merger that deliberately
preserves several of those
inconsistencies for archival
fidelity.
Readers should note that Site
ALPHA records retain the
DD.MM.YYYY date
convention of the desert
operations team, while Site
BETA logs use ISO 8601.
Currency figures appear in
the currency of expenditure
— rials, rupees or euros —
with the separator
conventions of the
originating office. Appendix
C provides the conversion
basis.
 «Two deserts of data
— one of sand, one of
 rain — and a single
 instrument:
 patience.»
Programme milestones of the
year include the completion
of aerosol transect T-7, the
first full-season operation of
the cyclone moorings at
BETA, and a 31 per cent
reduction in diesel
dependency at ALPHA.
Setbacks are reported with
equal candour: seventeen
sand-storm shutdowns, one
flooded cable trench, and the
loss of sonde T7-09 to a
fishing trawl.
This volume was compiled by
the Programme Office from
partner submissions received
before 12 January 2026. Late
corrections appear only in
the Annex reprint and are
flagged as non-authoritative.
— The Editors

3 · Desert Operations — Site ALPHA
Site ALPHA operates under the sand-storm shutdown protocol agreed with the regional partner. The
authoritative statement of the protocol, as lodged in Muscat, is reproduced below in the original
Arabic; no English translation is circulated.e3
 Statement 3-1 (Arabic, right-to-left; reproduced as submitted facsimile).
3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.
Crew rotations during the season were staged through the coastal airstrip rather than the desert
track, adding four hours to each rotation but avoiding convoy exposure during peak visibility events.
The protocol threshold (see Statement 3-1) was not breached during any rotation window.
3.1 Dust climatology
Monthly mean dust flux for both sites is mapped in Figure 3-2; the annual maximum at ALPHA
occurred in mid-summer, coincident with the strongest shamal episodes.

5.1 The June dust intrusion
The June maximum columnar aerosol optical depth at BETA reached 0.82 during the dust intrusion
of 14 June, the highest single-day value of the record (Figure 5-1).
The June median columnar aerosol optical depth at BETA remained 0.28 outside the intrusion
window, the lowest monthly median of the record.

12 · Station Diaries (extracts)
ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.
BETA, 14 June. — Sky the colour of unpolished brass all afternoon. Sun photometer needle
went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and
again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.
Insurance paperwork weighs more than the sonde did. — R.S.

12 · Station Diaries (extracts)
ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.
BETA, 14 June. — Sky the colour of unpolished brass all afternoon. Sun photometer needle
went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and
again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.
Insurance paperwork weighs more than the sonde did. — R.S.

3 · Desert Operations — Site ALPHA
Site ALPHA operates under the sand-storm shutdown protocol agreed with the regional partner. The
authoritative statement of the protocol, as lodged in Muscat, is reproduced below in the original
Arabic; no English translation is circulated.e3
 Statement 3-1 (Arabic, right-to-left; reproduced as submitted facsimile).
3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.

The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in

per cent between cleanings.

3 · Desert Operations — Site ALPHA
Site ALPHA operates under the sand-storm shutdown protocol agreed with the regional partner. The
authoritative statement of the protocol, as lodged in Muscat, is reproduced below in the original
Arabic; no English translation is circulated.e3
 Statement 3-1 (Arabic, right-to-left; reproduced as submitted facsimile).
3.0 Shamal season narrative
The summer shamal arrived eleven days earlier than the climatological median and persisted in
three pulses of six to nine days. Station operations adapted by shifting lidar maintenance to
pre-dawn windows and by pre-positioning the wash-water bowser at the dome apron. No instrument
damage was recorded during any pulse, although optical throughput on the ceilometer declined 8
per cent between cleanings.
Crew rotations during the season were staged through the coastal airstrip rather than the desert
track, adding four hours to each rotation but avoiding convoy exposure during peak visibility events.
The protocol threshold (see Statement 3-1) was not breached during any rotation window.
3.1 Dust climatology
Monthly mean dust flux for both sites is mapped in Figure 3-2; the annual maximum at ALPHA
occurred in mid-summer, coincident with the strongest shamal episodes.

The 2025 yearbook is the
second consolidated volume
covering both observatories
and the first to be compiled
under the joint
data-governance charter. It
merges what were, until last
year, two separately
circulated site reports with
incompatible conventions —
a merger that deliberately
preserves several of those
inconsistencies for archival
fidelity.
Readers should note that Site
ALPHA records retain the
DD.MM.YYYY date
convention of the desert
operations team, while Site
BETA logs use ISO 8601.
Currency figures appear in
the currency of expenditure
— rials, rupees or euros —
with the separator
conventions of the
originating office. Appendix
C provides the conversion
basis.
 «Two deserts of data
— one of sand, one of
 rain — and a single
 instrument:
 patience.»
Programme milestones of the
year include the completion
of aerosol transect T-7, the
first full-season operation of
the cyclone moorings at
BETA, and a 31 per cent
reduction in diesel
dependency at ALPHA.
Setbacks are reported with
equal candour: seventeen
sand-storm shutdowns, one
flooded cable trench, and the
loss of sonde T7-09 to a
fishing trawl.
This volume was compiled by
the Programme Office from
partner submissions received
before 12 January 2026. Late
corrections appear only in
the Annex reprint and are
flagged as non-authoritative.
— The Editors

ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.
BETA, 14 June. — Sky the colour of unpolished brass all afternoon. Sun photometer needle
went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and
again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.
Insurance paperwork weighs more than the sonde did. — R.S.

12 · Station Diaries (extracts)
ALPHA, 4 July. — Shut down at 09:40 local when the ridge vanished. Visibility meter read 310
before we lost the mast camera to static. Nine hours in the mess playing carrom; generator shed
104.5 units before the wind turned. Longest event of my three seasons. — K.A-B.
BETA, 14 June. — Sky the colour of unpolished brass all afternoon. Sun photometer needle
went places I have not seen outside the textbook; logged the column at 0.82 at half past two and
again at three. Fisherfolk stayed in; the harbourmaster called twice to check the flags. — S.M.
BETA, 14 October. — Trawler out of the northern grounds took T7-09 on descent, clean
through the chute lines. Skipper radioed apologetic; brought us pomfret by way of settlement.
Insurance paperwork weighs more than the sonde did. — R.S.
Diary extracts are informal and unedited; where they conflict with tables, tables govern.
